body.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal M_x(p_x)\) contains every Stoye spike vector \(s_a\). Then \(R_x(q,p_x)=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\{(1-q_a)U_{ax}-\sum_{c\neq a}q_cL_{cx}\}\) for every \(q\in\Delta_K\), so \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) and \(v_x(p_x)\) equal the allocation correspondence and value in Proposition 1 of Stoye2007ManyTreatments. For \(K=2\), the formula reduces to the standard binary fractional minimax-regret rule.
body.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and separates genuinely joint restrictions from the classical spike geometry.
body.gap: Stoye2007ManyTreatments assumes the spike states are available; the present statement derives his rule as the exact special case of a categorical-instrument identified polytope.
body.consumer: Decision theorists can reuse Stoye's closed-form allocation whenever the observable spike-feasibility certificates pass.
